name: the nameless city
facts: The narrator's fear was tied to first seeing the terrible valley and the nameless city under a cold moon.
The crawling reptiles referenced later belong to a race associated with the nameless city.

sources.quote: Suddenly there came another burst of that acute fear which had intermittently seized me ever since I first saw the terrible valley and the nameless city under a cold moon
the crawling reptiles of the nameless city

name: the abyss
facts: Sudden gusts of air rose around the mouth of the abyss each sunset and sunrise.
The narrator feared being swept bodily through the open gate into the phosphorescent abyss.
A horde of devil-like creatures was seen outlined against the luminous aether of the abyss.

sources.quote: I instantly recalled the sudden gusts which had risen around the mouth of the abyss each sunset and sunrise
I dropped prone again and clutched vainly at the floor for fear of being swept bodily through the open gate into the phosphorescent abyss.
Turning, I saw outlined against the luminous aether of the abyss what could not be seen against the dusk of the corridor

name: The Narrator
facts: He was seized by acute fear and sat up frantically, gazing back toward the tunnels leading to the outer world.
He heard a deep, low moaning sound growing in volume, the first sound to break the silence of the depths.
He became conscious of an increasing draft of cold air flowing from the tunnels and the city above.
He looked at his watch and saw that sunrise was near.
He braced himself to resist the gale sweeping down into the abyss.
He dropped prone and clutched at the floor for fear of being swept into the abyss.
He compared himself to the man who was torn to pieces by the nameless race.
He believed he screamed frantically and was almost mad.
He tried to crawl against the wind but was pushed slowly toward the unknown world.
His reason snapped and he babbled the couplet of the mad Arab Alhazred.
He saw a nightmare horde of devil-like reptile creatures outlined against the abyss.
He was plunged into darkness after the great brazen door clanged shut behind the creatures.
fate: He survived the ordeal, guided back to life by unknown means, but remains haunted, expecting to 'shiver in the night wind till oblivion—or worse—claims me.'

sources.quote: despite my exhaustion I found myself starting frantically to a sitting posture and gazing back along the black corridor toward the tunnels that rose to the outer world
I looked at my watch and saw that sunrise was near, so braced myself to resist the gale that was sweeping down to its cavern home
I dropped prone again and clutched vainly at the floor for fear of being swept bodily through the open gate into the phosphorescent abyss.
once more I compared myself shudderingly to the only human image in that frightful corridor, the man who was torn to pieces by the nameless race
I think I screamed frantically near the last—I was almost mad—but if I did so my cries were lost in the hell-born babel of the howling wind-wraiths.
Finally reason must have wholly snapped; for I fell to babbling over and over that unexplainable couplet of the mad Arab Alhazred, who dreamed of the nameless city
what Abaddon guided me back to life, where I must always remember and shiver in the night wind till oblivion—or worse—claims me
And as the wind died away I was plunged into the ghoul-peopled darkness of earth's bowels; for behind the last of the creatures the great brazen door clanged shut

name: Alhazred
facts: He was called the mad Arab.
He dreamed of the nameless city.
He is credited with an unexplainable couplet: 'That is not dead which can eternal lie, And with strange eons, even death may die.'

sources.quote: that unexplainable couplet of the mad Arab Alhazred, who dreamed of the nameless city
That is not dead which can eternal lie, And with strange eons, even death may die.

name: the nameless race
aliases: crawling reptiles of the nameless city
facts: The nameless race tore a man to pieces, as recalled by the narrator.
A nightmare horde of these creatures was described as hate-distorted, grotesquely panoplied, and half-transparent devils of a race no man might mistake.
Their voices took the articulate form of ghastly cursing and snarling of strange-tongued fiends.
They were the crawling reptiles of the nameless city.
The great brazen door clanged shut behind the last of the creatures.

sources.quote: the man who was torn to pieces by the nameless race

I heard the ghastly cursing and snarling of strange-tongued fiends. Turning, I saw outlined against the luminous aether of the abyss what could not be seen against the dusk of the corridor—a nightmare horde of rushing devils; hate-distorted, grotesquely panoplied, half-transparent devils of a race no man might mistake—the crawling reptiles of the nameless city.
behind the last of the creatures the great brazen door clanged shut with a deafening peal of metallic music
